To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a population pharmacokinetic (popPK) model was developed to characterize the pharmacokinetics of a novel extended-release formulation of methylphenidates (MPH-ER) in pediatric patients with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADH) and that a popPK/pharmacodynamic model showed that the MPH-ER dose, body weight and clinical response (ADHD Rating Scale [ADH-RS] scores) are related.
a population PK model for MPH-MLR was developed using data from healthy adults, which was then extended to children and adolescents with ADHD.
the pharmacokinetics and clinical effects of MPH-MLB are well characterized in healthy adult and pediatric patients with ADHD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a population pharmacokinetic/phamacodynamic model for the new extended-release MPH-MLR formulation in healthy adults and children and adolescents with ADHD.
the development of a population pharmacokinetic (PK) model for the MPH-MLR and a pharmacokinetic/pharmaco-dynamic model for MPH-MLR.
the development of a new multilayer formulation of extended-release MPH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pharmacokinetic model developed in this study adequately describes the pharmacokinetics of MPH-MLB in healthy adults and pediatric subjects with ADHD, and the pharmacokinetic/pharma-codynamic model developed in this work adequately describes the relationship between MPH-MLB plasma concentration and ADHD-RS-4 total scores in pediatric subjects with ADHD.
the population pharmacokinetics model developed using data from healthy adult and pediatric subjects with ADHD adequately described plasma concentration–time profiles in this population.
the pharmacokinetics of MPH-MLB in pediatric subjects are similar to that in adults and that the pharmacokinetic parameters are dependent upon body weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a population pharmacokinetic (PK) model for methylphenidate HCl multiple-layer beads (MPH-MSR) in children with ADHD and then used this model to predict the PK/PD relationship between MPH-MLR and ADHD symptom severity in this same population.
a two-compartment, first order, absorption model with lag time adequately described plasma concentration–time profiles of MPH-MLB in healthy subjects.

we have a population pharmacokinetic and pharmacokinetic/pharmocodynamic model that describes the pharmacokinetics of the new MPH-MLR formulation in pediatric subjects with ADHD, which may be useful for selecting the initial dose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can predict the concentration-time profiles of methylphenidates, and the effect on the clinical outcome, using the population pharmacokinetic/pharmaco-dynamic model.
the pharmacokinetics of MPH-MLB is similar to that of other extended-release formulations, but with a longer duration of action.
the population pharmacokinetic/pharmaco-dynamic model for MPH-MLR may be useful in the clinical setting to aid in dose selection for individual patients.
